sentences.text:
(Ex-parte)
 JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,
seeking compensation due to the death of Ramachandraiah in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners is as follows:-
That on 01-10-2024 at about 11-20 a.m., Ramachandraiah was riding the Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-52-U-9153 from Sirivara Hand Post towards Nagavalli village side and when he reached near Kumbhipalya Village, F.K.I Factory,
Nagavalli - K G Temple road, at that time the rider of Honda DIO Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HP-5523 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against Honda Activa Scooter of Ramachandraiah, result of which Ramachandraiah fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
So far, the petitioners have spent Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies.
3. Prior to the accident, Ramachandraiah was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 55 years.
He was working as a Mason, thereby earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the untimely death of deceased, petitioners are put to great mental shock and agony.
4. Respondent no.1/

the Insurer of Honda DIO Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HP-5523 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the claim petition is barred by limitation and that the rider of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and that the petitioners in collusion with the jurisdiction police have created false records to get the compensation.

The claim petition filed by the petitioners is liable to be dismissed for non joinder of Shivamma vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6358893/
2 necessary parties i.e., insured and insurer of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-U-9153.
5.

sentences.text: In spite of service of notice, the Respondent no.2 did not appear before this court.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues arise for the consideration of the court:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, Sri.Ramachandraiah succumbed to the injuries sustained in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 01-10-2024 at about 11-20 am., on Nagavalli- K G Temple road, near Kumbiapalaya village, KFI factory, Hebbur Hobli, Tumkur Taluk & District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HP-5523?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3
. What Order or Award?
7. The petitioner No.1 got examined himself as Pw1 and one witness is examined as PW.2 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.

On the other hand, the respondent no.1 has examined its legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.
8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative, Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-

Petitioners have categorically contended that, on 01-10-2024 at about 11-20 a.m.,
when Ramachandraiah (hereinafter called the deceased) was riding Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-52- U-9153 from Sirivara Hand Post towards Nagavalli village side and when he reached near Kumbhipalya Village, F.K.I Factory, Nagavalli - K G Temple road, at that time the rider of Honda DIO Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HP-5523 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against Honda Activa Scooter of deceased, result of which Ramachandraiah fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.

sentences.text:
In order to prove the petition averments, Petitioner no.1 who is the wife of deceased got examined herself as Pw.1 and produced in all 9 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.7 i.e., F.I.R with Complaint, Spot mahazar, Sketch, Inquest mahazar, Post mortem report, IMV report and Charge sheet etc., are the material documents to prove the present issue.
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by the son of deceased by name Shivaraju R, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.0189/2024 of Hebbur Police Station for the offence punishable under section 281, 106(1) of B.N.S.

The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 281, 106(1) of B.N.S.
13.
The petitioners have contended that, the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
In the light of the contention taken by the petitioners, if the spot mahazar is perused, the width of the road at the spot of the accident is nearly 18 ft.,
As per the case of the petitioners and as borne out by police records at the time of accident deceased was proceeding from Sirivara Hand post towards Nagavalli village.
The offending vehicle was proceeding on the opposite direction i.e., from Nagavalli village towards Sirivara Hand post.
The petitioners have produced Spot mahazar and Sketch.
If the Spot mahazar and Sketch is perused, the spot of the accident is on the left side of the road leads to Nagavalli village.
It means, the accident in question has occurred on the left side of Sirivara Hand post - Nagavalli village, in which road the deceased was proceeding.
Hence, it can be said that the rider of the offending vehicle by riding his vehicle from opposite direction took the vehicle towards the right side of his road and hit to the vehicle of the deceased.
It is true that, PW.1 is not an eye witness to the accident.
But, she has examined the eye witness to the accident as Pw.2.
In the Charge sheet, name of the Pw.2 finds place as an eye witness to the accident.

Though the respondent no.2 has denied the manner of accident, but they have not examined either the rider of the offending vehicle or any of the eye witness to the accident to rebut the evidence given by the Pw.1 and Pw.2.
Admittedly, Charge sheet is filed against the rider of the offending vehicle.
The respondent no.2 being the owner and even the rider of the offending vehicle have not challenged the Charge sheet.
Hence, without discussing much on this Point this court holds above Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
14. Issue no 2 :

It is the contention taken by the petitioners that, Petitioner No.1 being the wife,
Petitioner no.2 being the son and Petitioner no.3 being the daughter of the deceased are entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased and that deceased was working as a Mason and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
15.
As per the own evidence of Pw.1, Petitioner no.2 is doing Coolie work and he is residing separately with his family and Petitioner no.3 is the married daughter and residing in her matrimonial home.

The Pw.1 has clearly deposed that, Petitioner No.2 was not maintaining the family and PW.1 was wholly depending on the income of her husband and that Petitioner no.3 was not depending on the income of the deceased.

Under such circumstances, it can be said that though the Petitioner no.2 and 3 are the legal representative of the deceased as per Sec.8 of the Hindu Succession Act, but they are not the dependants of the deceased.

sentences.text: It is stated that at the time of accident, deceased was aged about 55 years.
The petitioners have not produced any authenticated documents to prove the age of the deceased.
In the PM report, age of the deceased is shown as 55 years.
The learned counsel for respondent no.1 has produced memo with xerox copy of the Ration card and Invitation card of the death ceremony of deceased.
If the said document is perused, the date of birth of deceased is mentioned as 18-10- 1962.
Hence, his court inclines to consider the age of the deceased as 62 years.

17. So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of petitioners,
deceased was working as a Mason and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the actual income and avocation of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident has occurred in the year 2024, court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.
Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- p.m.

[
18. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife, and she alone is the dependant of the deceased,  of the annual income is to be deducted towards personal expenses and remaining  is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.
19. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40%
of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case as the deceased was 62 years no future prospect can be considered.
20. Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/-, out of it if 50% is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased, it comes around Rs.8,250/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group over 62 year is '7'.
Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.6,93,000/- (Rs.8250 x 7 x 12 =6,93,000/-).
21. Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 lost her husband and petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their father, thereby lost the love and affection of deceased.

So far as the quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned, slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.

It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10%
in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

sentences.text:
As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.

23. In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/-
2 Transportation and funeral Rs. 18,150/-
expenses 3 Loss of spousal consortium, Rs.1,45,200/- parental consortium (Rs.48,400X3) 4 Loss of Dependency Rs.6,93,000/-
Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.8,74,500/- and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
24. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with the 1st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
25. The learned counsel for respondent no.1 has submitted that as on the date of accident the driver of the offending vehicle had no driving license .

26. If the charge sheet is perused, the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence u/Sec.181 of MV Act along with other Sections under BNS alleging inter alia that at the time of accident the driver was not holding valid driving license.
Further the owner of the offending vehicle was also charge sheeted u/Sec. 180 of IMV Act for his permiting the driver who had no driving license to drive the offending vehicle.

27. The petitioner has seriously refuted the said contention taken by the respondent no.1 and submitted that, as on the date of accident the driver was holding valid driving license to drive the offending vehicle and respondent no.1 in order to escape from the liability now contending that the driver was not holding valid driving license and that the respondent no.1 has not issued notice to the owner/respondent no.2 to produce the driving license of the driver of the offending vehicle and they have not examined the RTO to prove that the driver was not holding valid driving license, hence merely on the bald statement of the respondent no.1 it cannot be concluded that driver was not Shivamma vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6358893/
6 holding valid driving license.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that even if for any reason this court comes to the conclusion that the driver was not holding valid driving license then also at the first instance the respondent no.1 has to pay the compensation and to recover the amount from the respondent no.2 under pay and recovery.
28. In order to prove that the driver was not holding valid driving license, the respondent no.1 has relied upon charge sheet.

29. It is true that respondent no.1 has not issued notice to the respondent no.2 to produce the driving license of the driver of the offending vehicle and they have not examined the RTO to prove that as on the date of accident driver was not holding valid driving license but if the charge sheet is perused, the respondent no.2 being the owner has not furnished the particulars of the Driving license.

If really, the driving license of the driver was valid and was in force as on the date of accident, definitely the respondent no.2 would have furnished the particulars of the driving license of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further respondent no.2 on service of summons from the court has remained absent.
If really driving license was in force, then nothing prevented the respondent no.2 from producing the driving license of the driver of the motorcycle.

30. Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment relied by the learned counsel for respondent no.1 reported in SLP (Civil) NO.11757/2025 between Mahaveer Vs. The Branch Manager, United India Insurance Co.Ltd., & Ors.

entities.text: Mahaveer Vs. The Branch Manager, United India Insurance Co.Ltd., & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said case, it was the defence of the Insurance company that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess valid driving license,
hence they are not liable to pay the compensation.

It was observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that "it is neither for the Insurance company to prove the negative nor is it possible to presume based only on the charge sheet filed, the entrustment of the vehicle by the owner, which charge is on the rash and negligent driving of the driver.
What assumes significance is that despite the owner of the vehicle having been a party before the Tribunal, no evidence was given.
The owner did not mount the witness box nor was any license produced either of the person who was driving the vehicle or the person to whom it was entrusted.
The owner thus failed to prove that the vehicle was entrusted to a person having valid license.
31. Hence, from the materials placed on record it can be said that as on the date of accident the driver was not holding valid driving license.
The learned counsel for respondent no 1 has submitted that subsequent to the amendment no pay and recovery can be ordered.

It is submitted by the learned counsel that, the right to recover compensation from the owner of the offending vehicle flows from the proviso attached to sub section (4) of section 149 of M.V. Act 1988 has been omitted by Act of 2019 and therefore in case of a breach of policy, it is only the owner against whom award can be directly made and insurer is liable to be relieved from any liability to indemnify the owner.
32. The learned counsel at this juncture has refereed the judgment rendered in MFA No. 4739/2024 (MV-D) between Bhagyashree & Ors., Vs. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.Ltd., & Anr., .

entities.text: Bhagyashree & Ors., Vs. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.Ltd., & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case also the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid driving license as on the date of accident.
The Hon'ble High Court in the aforesaid case has observed that "subsequent to the amendement, the principal of pay and recover will not apply".
With that observation the Hon'ble Shivamma vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6358893/

33. Per contra the learned counsel for petitioners have submitted that even though accident in question was occurred subsequent to the amendment to MV Act but pay and recovery still be ordered against the Insurance Company.

34. On perusal of the document, the accident in question has occurred on 01-10-2024 i.e,
subsequent to the amendment dated 1-4-2022.

Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment rendered in Civil Appeal No.3593-94 of 2024 between Rajesh Mitra and another V/s Karnani Properties Ltd., wherein reference was made of case in Goutam Dey V/s Jyotsna Chetterji reported in 2012 Online Culcutta 642 wherein it was held that, "The New statute with touches upon the existing rights cannot be retrospective, without an express provision or necessary implication expressing the clear intent of the legislature".

entities.text: Goutam Dey V/s Jyotsna Chetterji reported in 2012 Online Culcutta 642
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was further observed that the enforcement of the new statute Ipso facto will not take away the rights already accrued under a repealed statute, unless this intention is reflected in the new statute.

35. Further in 2025 AFC 14110 between ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s Smt.Arti Devi and 8 others decided on 31-01-2025, in the said appeal question of law raised is in the light of motor vehicles (amendment) Act 2019, wherein question is also raised as to whether mere omission of proviso attached to sub section (4) of section 149 of M.V. Act 1988 after its replacement by section 150 by amendment Act 2019 would mean that, the liability of the insurer to pay and its right to recover the amount from the owner has been taken away and does not survive in relation to accident occurring after 1-4-2022.

entities.text: ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s Smt.Arti Devi and 8 others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble High court of judicature at Allahabad after elaborately discussing the purposive interpretation of statute, concept of pay and recovery, leading authority has arrived at the conclusion that "Mere omission of proviso attached to sub section (4) of Section 149 of M.V. Act 1988 after its replacement by section 150 of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act 2019,
neither takes away the liability of the insurer to pay the claimants nor its right to recover the said amount from the owner.

entities.text: High court of judicature at Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The law to this effect remains intact and un- effected by amendment Act 2019 and hence, insurer shall continue to indemnify the owner's risk in relation to accident taking place after 1-4-2022 and PAY AND RECOVER principle will still continue to govern the field advancing social object of the statute protecting third party interest.
The principle of law laid down by the Supreme Court in National Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s Swarna Singh and others has not lost its significance and binding effect despite omission of proviso".

entities.text: National Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s Swarna Singh and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

ICICI Lombard Nibhaye Vadde General Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pooja & Ors., In the said case also the accident in question was occurred subsequent to the amendment i.e., on 21-08- 2022 and in the said case also the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid driving license to drive the vehicle.

Therefore, the Hon'ble High Court has directed the Shivamma vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6358893/

37. The learned counsel for petitioners have argued that, even if section 149 (4) of M.V. Act is omitted but there is no specific reference in the amendment to M.V. Act dated 1-4-2022 regarding deletion of the principle of pay and recovery.

38. So far as the judgment relied by the learned counsel for respondent no.1 referred above rendered by the Hon'ble High Court is concerned, it is true that in the said case because of the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid driving license, the owner of the offending vehicle was made liable to pay the compensation.

But the Learned counsel for petitioners has produced Daily orders of Hon'ble High Court in MFA No. 4739/2024 wherein after the passing of the judgment, memo is made by the petitioner and matter was posted "for being spoken to".

In the memo it was submitted that the issue with regard to the amendement, whether it is with reference to the policy or accident,
the same is pending before the Division Bench which is coming up on 10-01-2026.
In view of the same, the Hon'ble High Court has recalled the judgment dated 06-11-2025.

Hence, it can be said that the judgment passed in MFA No. 4739/2024 dated 06-11- 2025 cannot be considered as same is set aside by the very same court.
39.
In the present case it is proved by the respondent no.1 that as on the date of accident, the driver had no valid driving license to drive the vehicle and thereby there is breach of policy condition.

But by relying upon the observation made in the aforesaid judgments, this court orders the Insurance company to pay the compensation amount and then to recover the amount from the owner under the principle of pay and recovery.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.1 this court directs the respondent no.1 to pay compensation to the petitioners along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount and to recover the said amount from the Respondent no.2.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
40. Issue No.3 :- In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 & 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners are hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,74,500/- + cost of Rs.1000/- imposed vide order on IA No.II.
In all the petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.8,75,500/- (Rupees Eight Lakh Seventy Five Thousand Five Hundred only).
A Sum of Rs.8,74,500/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,
seeking compensation due to the death of Ramachandraiah in a road traffic accident.
The respondent no.2 has contended that the claim petition is barred by limitation and that the rider of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and that the petitioners in collusion with the jurisdiction police have created false records to get the compensation.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.
opennyai_summary.issue:
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues arise for the consideration of the court:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that, Sri.Ramachandraiah succumbed to the injuries sustained in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 01-10-2024 at about 11-20 am., on Nagavalli- K G Temple road, near Kumbiapalaya village, KFI factory, Hebbur Hobli, Tumkur Taluk & District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HP-5523?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3
. What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 281, 106(1) of B.N.S.
13.
The petitioners have contended that, the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, it can be said that the rider of the offending vehicle by riding his vehicle from opposite direction took the vehicle towards the right side of his road and hit to the vehicle of the deceased.
But, she has examined the eye witness to the accident as Pw.2.
The Pw.1 has clearly deposed that, Petitioner No.2 was not maintaining the family and PW.1 was wholly depending on the income of her husband and that Petitioner no.3 was not depending on the income of the deceased.
Under such circumstances, it can be said that though the Petitioner no.2 and 3 are the legal representative of the deceased as per Sec.8 of the Hindu Succession Act, but they are not the dependants of the deceased.

4 16.
17. So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of petitioners,
deceased was working as a Mason and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the actual income and avocation of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident has occurred in the year 2024, court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.
Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- p.m.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.6,93,000/- (Rs.8250 x 7 x 12 =6,93,000/-).
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.
Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.1 this court directs the respondent no.1 to pay compensation to the petitioners along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount and to recover the said amount from the Respondent no.2.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
40. Issue No.3 :- In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 & 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners are hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,74,500/- + cost of Rs.1000/- imposed vide order on IA No.II.
In all the petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.8,75,500/- (Rupees Eight Lakh Seventy Five Thousand Five Hundred only).
A Sum of Rs.8,74,500/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award and to recover the said amount from the respondent no.2/owner of the offending vehicle.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.7,78,700/- Petitioner No.2 and 3 are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each
Out of the amount, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner on proper identification through E-payment.
So far as the amount apportioned to the petitioners no 2 and 3 are concerned same is ordered to be released in their favour after due identification through E - payment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
